claims.text: High-temperature multicomponent HEAs near melting exhibit solid and liquid phases with complex atomic configurations.
Traditional EAM references cannot capture the full diversity of configurations in the ab initio HEA liquid.
The EAM reference should be replaced by a deep-learning interatomic potential trained on ab initio MD liquid configurations.
A DNN trained solely on liquid configurations will sample a broader and more accurate range of atomic configurations than an EAM reference.
A DNN potential can describe both solid and liquid structures in high-entropy carbonitrides.
The cited DeepMD potential was trained on DFT calculations to describe both liquid and solid high-entropy carbonitride phases.
The DNN provides an improved potential-energy surface that captures a wider spectrum of local environments and dynamic liquid fluctuations.
Learning directly from ab initio configurations allows the DNN to represent the configurational diversity of the liquid more faithfully.
The improved DNN fidelity will increase reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD using EAM references.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will decrease by approximately 20–30%.
The method is applicable to refractory or high-melting HEAs at approximately 3000–3600 K.
The applicable composition range includes systems similar to high-entropy Ti-Zr-Ta-Hf-Nb carbonitrides.
The melting temperature of (TiZrTaHfNb)C0.75N0.25 is 3580 ± 30 K.
The performance gain may disappear for compositions far from the training regime.
The performance gain may disappear if the ab initio training set lacks sufficient diversity.
DNN and EAM thermodynamic-integration calculations should be compared on the same representative HEA and benchmarked against direct ab initio free-energy calculations.
Failure to improve phase-space overlap or to reduce path mismatch by approximately 20–30% would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The proposed model is trained solely on liquid configurations but is presented as a replacement for calculations involving both solid and liquid phases. The cited DeepMD example instead used DFT training intended to describe both phases, so it does not validate the liquid-only training restriction.
